name: getpriority
synopsis: int setpriority(int which, id_t who, int prio);
description: getpriority() retrieves the scheduling priority (nice value) of a specified process, process group, or user. setpriority() sets the scheduling priority for the specified entities. The nice value affects process scheduling, with lower values indicating higher priority.

parameters.name: which
parameters.description: Specifies the type of entity: PRIO_PROCESS for a process, PRIO_PGRP for a process group, or PRIO_USER for a user

parameters.name: who
parameters.description: The identifier for the entity; 0 denotes the calling process, process group, or real user ID depending on which

return_value.success: Returns the nice value (which may be negative) on success
return_value.failure: Returns -1 on error and sets errno

errors.description: The caller attempted to set a lower nice value without required privilege
The which value is not one of PRIO_PROCESS, PRIO_PGRP, or PRIO_USER
The effective user ID does not match and the caller lacks privilege
No process was found matching the which and who values

bugs: According to POSIX, the nice value is a per-process setting, but under Linux/NPTL, it is a per-thread attribute, allowing different threads in the same process to have different nice values.
versions: First appeared in 4.2BSD; variations in Linux kernels, such as changes from Linux 2.6.12
